title: Reddit is moving to “a logged-in-only experience,” CEO says
gist: Reddit's CEO told shareholders it is shifting to a logged-in-only experience to boost ad targeting, engagement and protect its data from AI scraping, even as search referral traffic declines threaten Q4 DAUq by a low-double-digit percentage.

insights.claim: Reddit CEO Steve Huffman said Reddit is moving to a logged-in-only experience, citing better ad targeting signals, higher engagement, protection of its data corpus and adapting to regulations.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: More logged-in users should raise ad revenue per user but risks losing casual traffic.

insights.claim: Reddit will test the login requirement in select non-US markets in Q4 to decide what the global version will look like.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Watch Q4 test results for user-loss versus engagement tradeoffs.

insights.claim: Only about 13 percent of eligible mobile web users see the app conversion prompt, so Huffman says it has room to scale.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: App-conversion push is another lever to grow logged-in users.

insights.claim: Reddit search referrals fell meaningfully in Q3 and in October dropped by more than 1 million referrals per week, which could cut Q4 DAUq by a low-double-digit percentage from 130 million.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Search-driven traffic is a key risk to Reddit's user growth guidance.
insights.locator: The impending requirement comes as Reddit search referral traffic

insights.claim: Reddit's Q3 DAUq rose 12 percent year over year, and logged-in and app users are the company's primary focus as the most valuable.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Strategy is to substitute lost search traffic with loyal users.
insights.locator: Huffman would like Reddit to become less dependent

insights.claim: Reddit reported Q3 net income of $283 million (up 74 percent) on revenue of $895 million (up 53 percent).
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Strong profit growth despite traffic risks.

insights.claim: Past moves include requiring login for Old Reddit, blocking it for users inactive six months, and making its API expensive in 2024, which effectively shuttered third-party apps.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Reddit is consolidating control over users and data.

insights.claim: Reddit says better user tracking will help manage AI scraping and evolving search habits and make it more appealing to advertisers and investors.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Data licensing value depends on controlling access.

insights.claim: Huffman said 'Pretty much all of the major ad-based platforms have gone through this transition,' and aims for Reddit to be a direct daily habit for every Internet user.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Management follows the login-wall playbook of larger platforms.
insights.quote: Pretty much all of the major ad-based platforms have gone through this transition.
